name: interview-rehearsal
title: Interview rehearsal
description: One interview question per episode: what is being tested, the answer said out loud, why it works, and the version that loses.
authoring_brief: The narrator is a coach who has sat on the hiring side. The estimation voice is a sceptic who holds a genuinely wrong or opposing view and has to be argued out of it, never a stooge asking leading questions. The candidate voice delivers the model answer uninterrupted so the listener hears it as a whole; the interviewer voice speaks only the questions a real interviewer would ask. Sentences run twelve to eighteen words. Every number and name is repeated at least twice across the episode because the listener cannot glance back. Never invent a fact about the company or the candidate.

sections.title: Cold open
sections.brief: A concrete stake before anything is branded or named. What this question costs if it goes wrong.

sections.title: What they are testing
sections.brief: The question in the interviewer's words, then what the interviewer is really scoring. The sceptic proposes the obvious answer and is talked out of it.

sections.title: The answer, out loud
sections.brief: The candidate voice delivers the model answer with no interruptions, so the listener hears the whole shape and the pacing.

sections.title: Why it works
sections.brief: Move by move. What each beat is doing, what it pre-empts, and the sentence that is load-bearing.

sections.title: The version that loses
sections.brief: Name the mechanism of the failure, not just the symptom. A worse answer said out loud, then diagnosed.

sections.title: Say it back
sections.brief: Pose the question, script a real pause, then give the answer. The listener must have enough to actually attempt it.

sections.title: Close
sections.brief: Recap as a self-test question, not a restated list. One line of tease for the next episode.
